utterances.text: Thank you. Can we now look at the same map again, Exhibit 156? Without the markings, of course. Thank you. And you can see the map now. Could you please take the pen again? Can you mark with the number 1 the position where the silo was? And can you please also place a cross next to the number?

utterances.speaker: VILIM KARLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks].

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Could you please indicate Pionirska Street again, which is what you did yesterday?

utterances.speaker: VILIM KARLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I'm not sure exactly where it was, but I can indicate the general area, like I said yesterday.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: Can you please place the number 2 next to that spot and put a circle around the number 2.

utterances.speaker: VILIM KARLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks].

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Also in the statement you provided to the Prosecutor on the 7th of September, 1995, on page 2, paragraph 9; English version, page 2, paragraph 9. I'm going to give you the statements if you ask for them and if you disagree that that's what is stated in the statement. But you stated that you occasionally went to help out at certain positions; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: VILIM KARLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: Could you kindly indicate the positions that you went to? Can you also mark them with lines whenever it was that you went to help out units that were out in the field?

utterances.speaker: VILIM KARLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I don't know, because I never went to such places.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: You didn't go. All right. You said yesterday that you went to the hospital on a number of occasions before you ended up there, ultimately. On the way to the hospital, and as you were going to the Pionirska Ulica position, can you indicate other positions where the Croatian forces were?

utterances.speaker: VILIM KARLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: There is no way I can orient myself and mark these positions at this point in time.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: What about the MUP forces?

utterances.speaker: VILIM KARLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The same thing there.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I think yesterday we admitted as an exhibit something similar. If not, then could we tender this into evidence? I think that the Prosecutor asked something similar. I am just leaving it up to you, Your Honours, to see whether this can be admitted again as an exhibit or not.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: We are checking back, Mr. Borovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I think that it was, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: Your Honour, if I can assist, similar markings were made to a similar Prosecution exhibit yesterday, but we have no objection of it being tendered again.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: We will have it twice, Mr. Borovic. This will be received.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, this will be exhibit number 297.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: We will go back to position number 1 where the silo was. My question is: Did you have a sniper's nest at the silo?

utterances.speaker: VILIM KARLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. You said that there were ammunition depots at the silo?

utterances.speaker: VILIM KARLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: What kind of weapons were stored there?

utterances.speaker: VILIM KARLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I know we had infantry weapons and ammunition stored there. And as far as I can remember, we had smaller calibre mortars of 60 millimetres. That's all I can remember. Perhaps there were other weapons, but this is all I can remember.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Were -- did members of other units come to be issued with weapons from your silo?

utterances.speaker: VILIM KARLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that is correct. We were not issuing the weapons. We had nothing to do with that.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. You, as a member of the military, are you making an assessment that there, by the silo, had the status of a military facility?

utterances.speaker: VILIM KARLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I've already said that, the silo had strategic importance. Nobody's disputing that.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. When you described your positions towards the Danube river, when you said there was no infantry fighting, as you described it, and when you said that artillery was firing from the other side, what was your assignment at that point in time, until the infantry fighting or combat? What were you doing?

utterances.speaker: VILIM KARLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: We were just observing and monitoring the Danube.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. At the time when there were combat lines or defence lines, as you term it, in Vukovar, the ones that you drew and you don't know where these other lines were, across from that, across from the Danube there was the army, or there were soldiers. My question is: In the centre of Vukovar, or within the lines of defence of the Croatian forces, were there any Serb forces? So behind or within the Croatian army defence lines, were there any Serb soldiers there?

utterances.speaker: VILIM KARLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know. I can even say that I don't really understand exactly what you're asking me.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: Well, I'll try to clarify that. You had Vukovar defence lines. Was there any Serb military within those lines, not part of the ZNG or anything, but as members of a force with which you were in conflict?

utterances.speaker: VILIM KARLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I've already said who we were in conflict with, who we were fighting against. I don't know whether, at the time of the defence of the town, such units had infiltrated the lines or were inside of town. I don't know that.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. So there were no military activities by Serb forces within your lines in Vukovar?

utterances.speaker: VILIM KARLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I said I didn't know. I couldn't be everywhere in Vukovar, you understand.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: Besides the Croatian population, was there any Serb population intermingled there behind the lines of defence in Vukovar, the area that you covered?

utterances.speaker: VILIM KARLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I really don't know. I really -- I think that there were. I mean, I couldn't be sure about it, but I know that there were Serbs and Croats within -- or as part of that population.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: According to your information, could Serb civilians leave Vukovar, passing through your lines? Was that possible or not?

utterances.speaker: VILIM KARLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't have information about that, no.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: You said that you had hand-held launchers which were disposable?

utterances.speaker: VILIM KARLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: Once you use hand-held launcher, where were you issued with another one?

utterances.speaker: VILIM KARLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: We were not issued with another one.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. What happened, you would fire one shell, and that was the end of the war?

utterances.speaker: VILIM KARLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, you responded to that question yourself. I don't know what to answer. I don't know how to behave or what to say to that question. It's not the end of the war, but we ran out of shells.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. On page 10, line 8 -- could the usher please give you all of your statements, and if you disagree with something you will easily find it. You have statements here in the Dokmanovic case, the Ovcara case, and also your statements you gave to the Prosecutor in The Hague. On page 10, line 8 of the Belgrade trial you said, on the 13th of September, 2002, you said the following: That you held some sort of positions around the hospital. This is in Croatia. Is this correct?

utterances.speaker: VILIM KARLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: Do you confirm that answer?

utterances.speaker: VILIM KARLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. How many of you held these lines around the hospital? How many soldiers were there altogether?

utterances.speaker: VILIM KARLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Perhaps seven or eight people in the group of mine.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. What are those positions around the hospital? Can you describe them in more detail because we weren't there?

utterances.speaker: VILIM KARLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I've already said that we were withdrawing towards the centre of the town, and before we completely fell apart we were there at those lines which were close to the hospital.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: How far from the hospital?

utterances.speaker: VILIM KARLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: About 100 metres.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: What sort of weapons did you use to guard the positions around the hospital? Did you also have automatic rifles and mortar shells?

utterances.speaker: VILIM KARLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: First of all, I would like to correct you. We're not talking about mortar shells. We are only had rifles.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: Did you have Zoljas?

utterances.speaker: VILIM KARLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, we didn't have any Zoljas.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: Not you, but the others.

utterances.speaker: VILIM KARLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know. I really can't remember. I have no idea.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: Do you allow for the possibility that the others had Zoljas and hand-grenades?

utterances.speaker: VILIM KARLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, it would be all right to allow for the possibility. Perhaps they did have them and perhaps they didn't. I simply don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: Also on page 10, lines 8 to 11, you said that an ultimatum was issued, that not a single bullet could any longer be fired from the hospital compound?

utterances.speaker: VILIM KARLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: Who issued that order?

utterances.speaker: VILIM KARLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It doesn't state in these statements that I had gone to see a couple of -- my men who were wounded, so I had information from them. I no longer had any superiors. We were no longer organised in our resistance. So I learned this information from the hospital. I found out this information from the hospital, the information you are talking about, and then I said that in my statement.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Who issued the ultimatum to the hospital, to the people there, saying that not a single bullet should -- could be fired from the hospital?

utterances.speaker: VILIM KARLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know about that.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: But you heard that such an ultimatum existed and that after that no other ammunition was fired from the hospital perimeter?

utterances.speaker: VILIM KARLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not from the hospital.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: That's what it says here.

utterances.speaker: VILIM KARLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: You are saying about no bullets being fired from the hospital.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: Well, that's what it says there.

utterances.speaker: VILIM KARLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It's not from the hospital. It's from the direction of the hospital.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: Just a minute, please. I'm being very patient. I read this out slowly. You mentioned positions yourself, positions around the hospital. And then further on you said that there was an ultimatum stating that not a single bullet could be fired from the perimeter of the hospital. Perimeter could not be 200 metres.

utterances.speaker: VILIM KARLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, perhaps I wasn't fully precise when stating that. When I said "perimeter," I meant the positions where we were. We were not to fire from that area any longer.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: Why not?

utterances.speaker: VILIM KARLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Because there was an ultimatum stating that the hospital would be attacked by air-raids dropping napalm bombs that would kill everybody.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: If you fired from the hospital perimeter?

utterances.speaker: VILIM KARLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: From the hospital direction.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Do you know who Harlan von Bassinger is? Did you hear that name?

utterances.speaker: VILIM KARLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: Can you tell the Court who he is?

utterances.speaker: VILIM KARLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is a man who was from Zagreb who had come with me to Vukovar. He was wounded in Vukovar, and as far as I know, he is listed as missing to this day.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: Andreas Lehpamer?

utterances.speaker: VILIM KARLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think that this man lives to -- in Samobor to this day. He was born there, grew up in Samobor. He was wounded gravely. He had also come there with me.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: Were there foreign nationals in your units of what you called Croatian army and, if so, what do you know about that?

utterances.speaker: VILIM KARLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In my unit, we did not have a single foreign national. I must add, though, that Harlan von Bassinger is not the real name of this person.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: Well, I'm discussing foreign nationals in general. Do you know whether there were any foreign nationals in the Croatian army?

utterances.speaker: VILIM KARLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think that there were, but none in my unit.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. You changed your uniform and discarded your weapon where?

utterances.speaker: VILIM KARLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In a house near the hospital.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: How far from the hospital?

utterances.speaker: VILIM KARLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: 150 to 200 metres.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Domazet asked you something similar about changing your uniform. This has to do with your statement given to the OTP, page 3, paragraph 3. He put it to you that all others were told to take off military uniforms and put on civilian clothes. This was at the hospital. How many soldiers there were, those who had been ordered to change their uniforms and leave their weapons?

utterances.speaker: VILIM KARLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: Do you know -- or did you see who gave them civilian clothes?

utterances.speaker: VILIM KARLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I didn't see that.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: Yesterday you said something similar to what you said in your OTP statement, namely, that you left the barracks either 2.00 or 3.00 p.m.; is that right?

utterances.speaker: VILIM KARLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Something like that.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: You also said that the beating at Ovcara lasted from 3.00 until 6.00 p.m. Is that possible?

utterances.speaker: VILIM KARLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it's possible that I said that.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. How late was it approximately when you came to Modateks after Ovcara?

utterances.speaker: VILIM KARLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I oriented myself on the amount of light. That's how I concluded that it was about 5.30 when we left Ovcara, but -- because it was beginning to get dark.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: So when did you then leave Ovcara?

utterances.speaker: VILIM KARLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know. Could have been 8.00 or 7.00. It's hard to pin-point time. These are all just rough assessment.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: Yes. And you are being quite fair about it. You also said that leading the column of buses was a vehicle called Pinzgauer?

utterances.speaker: VILIM KARLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: As a soldier, can you describe this vehicle to us? Can you describe it in greater detail? What did it look like? You said that it was an all-terrain vehicle. What else can you tell us about it?

utterances.speaker: VILIM KARLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know how else to describe it to you, its features. Are you interested in the power of its motor? It's an all-terrain vehicle used for communication, for medical purposes, for personnel transportation.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: Does it have benches on both sides in the back to transport soldiers?

utterances.speaker: VILIM KARLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, military people know that it can be customised to your needs. It can have benches, it can have something else.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: How many people can it carry?

utterances.speaker: VILIM KARLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: At least six.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: How about 10?

utterances.speaker: VILIM KARLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, impossible. I don't think it can carry 10. Maybe if they are crunched inside.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: I think they can carry 10 people, because I was in that vehicle myself. Was it vehicle -- was that vehicle covered in the back?

utterances.speaker: VILIM KARLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't remember. I don't even know how many people were inside.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: All right. This vehicle is bigger than a jeep, right? Pinzgauer is bigger than a jeep?

utterances.speaker: VILIM KARLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Perhaps a bit. It's not as big inside, but it is big.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: You, as a military expert, somebody who had training, would be able to confirm that it's bigger than a Campagnola?

utterances.speaker: VILIM KARLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know what a Campagnola is.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: Is it bigger?

utterances.speaker: VILIM KARLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I have no idea what a Campagnola is.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: Okay. That's fine. You claim that it was a Pinzgauer, so let's leave it at that. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: VILIM KARLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I remember that vehicle.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: In the Dokmanovic case, you stated as follows: "When we arrived there," and you are referring to Ovcara, "I saw JNA soldiers and Chetniks, the same ones who had been in the barracks." Is that right?

utterances.speaker: VILIM KARLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: Since you came out from the fourth bus and you told us who was there in front of the hangar, in your view. So please tell us this: The persons whom you noticed in the barracks, was Stuka also there, the person whom you later saw at Ovcara?

utterances.speaker: VILIM KARLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't remember Stuka from the barracks. I only remember him from the barracks [as interpreted].

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: All right. The statement that you gave to the OTP here in The Hague, on page 4, last paragraph, on page 4. English version, page 5, paragraph 4. Have you found this last paragraph? The one that was marked. I marked it to make it easier for you. You said this: As you were waiting to go through the gauntlet, and several groups had gone through the gauntlet before you, a soldier approached you asking you where you were from. Is that what it says there?

utterances.speaker: VILIM KARLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: My question: Did this soldier address anyone else but you?

utterances.speaker: VILIM KARLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't remember that. I don't remember that detail. Perhaps he did, perhaps he didn't.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: All right. Your friend Kemo, do you know how long he had lived in Ruma?

utterances.speaker: VILIM KARLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I know that he had lived there forever. That was his nickname.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: When was the last time you saw him?

utterances.speaker: VILIM KARLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Probably when we worked together. Before the war in 1989, or perhaps 1990.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. And you never saw him afterwards; is that right?

utterances.speaker: VILIM KARLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: Fine. What did you and Kemo do before the war? What did you trade in?

utterances.speaker: VILIM KARLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, if you have time, I can explain that. I lived in a family that was quite poor.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: What did you trade with?

utterances.speaker: VILIM KARLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: We traded the goods from Istanbul. We used to buy goods there quite cheaply and then bring them back home and then resell them.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: All right. How much time elapsed from when you left your bus until you entered the gauntlet?

utterances.speaker: VILIM KARLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can't remember. I can only give you an estimate. I believe it was around 15 minutes.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: Fine. Thank you. And during that time you observed what was going on in front of you; is that right?

utterances.speaker: VILIM KARLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, to the extent that I was able to observe.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: All right. Mr. Domazet asked you whether in addition to the people who were in the gauntlet there were other people and how many, and you gave a different answer from the one you gave in Belgrade at the trial there.

utterances.speaker: VILIM KARLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, listen, when it comes to figures, these estimates can differ because these are just estimates, and I'm not rehearsing it in advance in order to give the same figures every time.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: All right. If we put aside the people who are in the gauntlet, and if we assume that you are observing what's going on in front of you between the bus and the hangar, in that area between where you stood and the gauntlet, or where the entrance in the hangar was, were there a hundred people, 50 people, or could there have been 500, 600, 700 people?

utterances.speaker: VILIM KARLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Where? Which people?

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: All of the people who stood there between you and the gauntlet.

utterances.speaker: VILIM KARLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, there's no way there could have been five or 600. Once again, this is my assessment.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: And there could not have been 1.000 people there either; is that right?

utterances.speaker: VILIM KARLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, logically if I say that there were not 500 people there, then there could not have been 1.000 either.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: In Belgrade at the trial you said that you knew somebody called Mujidza. Who is Mujidza?

utterances.speaker: VILIM KARLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, that's precisely the nickname I could not remember yesterday. The nickname is Mujidza, or Mujidzon.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: The interpreters didn't hear what the witness said.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: Where?

utterances.speaker: VILIM KARLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: There. Actually, they were together practically the whole time while Stuka talked to me, and then they took us to Velepromet together.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, the interpreters didn't hear the last bit of the witness's answer, so could I ask him to repeat it?

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: Where did you see this person called Mujidza.

utterances.speaker: VILIM KARLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I saw him at Ovcara with Stuka.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: Where?

utterances.speaker: VILIM KARLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Both in the gauntlet and later. He used to guard us together with Stuka.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, could we put Exhibit 256 on the screen. Page 22, please. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: Would you please take the pen, and can the usher please assist the witness? Witness, would you please draw the lines depicting where the buses stood in relation to the hangar?

utterances.speaker: VILIM KARLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: You want me to draw the lines?

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: Yes. The lines showing where buses number 1, 2, 3, 4 and 5 stood.

utterances.speaker: VILIM KARLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks].

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Now, would you please put number 1 at the end of those lines and circle it, after the fifth line. Would you please do that?

utterances.speaker: VILIM KARLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks].

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Now, please, indicate with a cross the place where you saw Stuka for the first time.

utterances.speaker: VILIM KARLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks].

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: Could you put number 2 there and circle it?

utterances.speaker: VILIM KARLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks].

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: Just put number 2 outside of the circle. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: VILIM KARLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks].

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: And can you circle number 2?

utterances.speaker: VILIM KARLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks].

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Now, please, indicate with number 3 the location where Stuka guarded you.

utterances.speaker: VILIM KARLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks].

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: Put a cross there, and then number 3 next to it and circle it?

utterances.speaker: VILIM KARLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks]. This pen is not quite accurate.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: When you left the bus for the first time, where was your bus? Is it where you drew the fourth line, is that where your bus was?

utterances.speaker: VILIM KARLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: As far as I remember, the bus drove closer, a bit closer, because later on the buses left down the road.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: All right. From the fourth bus to the spot where you saw Stuka for the first time, did you get there when walking in a column, or how?

utterances.speaker: VILIM KARLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, for a while we actually stood there. It seems to me that the bus before us and our bus unloaded together, at the same time.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: All right. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, can this be admitted into evidence before we lose it from the screen and then I'll put my next question.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: It will be received.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, this will be exhibit number 298.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: Can you tell us, from your bus, that was the fourth bus shown here with line number 4, from there to the entrance into the hangar, what's the distance?

utterances.speaker: VILIM KARLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: From the fourth bus; is that right?

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: VILIM KARLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: 70 to 100 metres.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. From the place where the fourth bus was to where Stuka was, you could see only him and the soldiers as you approached that place?

utterances.speaker: VILIM KARLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Can you ask that again?

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: Well, tell us, what did you see once you left the fourth bus?

utterances.speaker: VILIM KARLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I've already described that. I could see the hangar entrance, I could see soldiers standing behind the buses next to the road. And then when I stood in front of the hangar, I saw the same soldiers again, standing on the other side of the road.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: All right. Thank you. Does this mean that once you left the bus you saw the soldiers and Stuka there in the same place where you later talked?

utterances.speaker: VILIM KARLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, no, no. Stuka came, he wasn't there. He wasn't waiting there. He came. They talked among themselves and to those who stood next to the bus, and then he came to the place where I was.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: All right. Thank you. From this part where you were, once you left the fourth bus, were you able to see Stuka in the gauntlet beating people or not?

utterances.speaker: VILIM KARLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I didn't see him, and I never said I did.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: When you went into the gauntlet after this conversation, my question is: Did Stuka follow you and did he enter the gauntlet and beat you with the rest of them or not?

utterances.speaker: VILIM KARLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't remember that. I think that he stayed behind me. He didn't go through the gauntlet together with me.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. You said that when you were taken out after that, when you were taken out of the hangar and you described it all, I don't want to take you back through all of that. That throughout that time, and at least an hour, Stuka was outside with you who was guarding you. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: VILIM KARLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: Did any one of the military personnel come during that period and issue orders to Stuka that he was to go somewhere else or not?

utterances.speaker: VILIM KARLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't remember.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: But when you say he was there the whole time, does that mean that he did not go to do some other duties during that hour?

utterances.speaker: VILIM KARLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't remember that he went to other assignments. He could have moved away a couple of metres from us, he entered the hangar and came out. It wasn't only him who was there. And he wasn't with us the whole time.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. You also said when you were asked by the Defence about Modateks that Stuka said already at the barracks that you would be taken to a place where you could easily go to Croatia. The question is: Was it your impression that this was a fact that was known to him already at Ovcara?

utterances.speaker: VILIM KARLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I didn't. I didn't even think about that. I just hoped that he was right.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: And later when you were already at Velepromet did you know that people were already going to Zagreb? I think you talk about -- talked about that yesterday. And that led you to the conclusion that he did send you to the right place after all?

utterances.speaker: VILIM KARLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, yes, I can agree with you. It's possible that it was like that.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: Today do you know the name of Ilija or Stuka? Is that his real name?

utterances.speaker: VILIM KARLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is my main problem, because at the time when he told me that his name was Stuka, I asked him, "What is your real name." He said Ilija. Later I found out that Stuka is actually a person with another name. I don't know exactly what the story is.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. On page 6, paragraph 4 of the statement you gave here to the Prosecutor, English version page 6, paragraph 8, you said when you left Ovcara towards Velepromet out of the six of you in the van you only remembered the name -- or you only remembered Berghofer. Do you agree that that is what is stated in your statement?

utterances.speaker: VILIM KARLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: When did you find out who the others were, and did you find out who the others were by the time you got to Velepromet?

utterances.speaker: VILIM KARLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I have learned about it gradually. I already knew some people. For example, Perkovic, who was with us, I knew him because he was brought out after his name was called out. The others I found out about later. Even about Berghofer I found out later. I didn't know about him at the time.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: Did you learn about Berghofer in Zagreb?

utterances.speaker: VILIM KARLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it's possible.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. If your memory serves you well, would you be able to describe where each person sat in this vehicle in which you left Ovcara to go to Modateks -- actually, you left in the direction of Velepromet. Where was Stuka, where was he sitting?

utterances.speaker: VILIM KARLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can't remember that. I know that someone was sitting out in the front with the driver, but I don't know whether it was him or somebody else.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Did Stuka have a weapon in that vehicle? Do you remember that? Did he bring a weapon with him?

utterances.speaker: VILIM KARLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I know that he had one the whole time. As to whether he had one in the vehicle or not, that's a little bit hazy, that part in the vehicle.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. In response to my learned colleague Domazet's question saying that you had to go back, you said that you didn't know, but you said that they went back to Ovcara; is that correct? Three soldiers were in uniform, only Stuka was not in uniform; is that correct? Of those people who were returning, actually who were leaving Modateks; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: VILIM KARLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Stuka was only different because he had this jacket. That's why I remembered him. Because he had this distinctive spitfire jacket.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: Did he have yellow Borovo boots on his feet?

utterances.speaker: VILIM KARLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Perhaps he did, and perhaps he didn't. I don't really remember it any longer.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: When, and you said this in your statement, he suggested that you swap your yellow Borovo boots, and then you said that he gave you a jacket and boots, did he maybe take your boots?

utterances.speaker: VILIM KARLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know, perhaps he did and perhaps he didn't. I really don't remember that anymore.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. How did you find out that people were called Belgija, Cedo? Did they introduce themselves or how did you find that out?

utterances.speaker: VILIM KARLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, as far as I can remember, Belgija introduced himself to me; and as for Cedo, I knew that he was being called that nickname.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: How did you find out about these others, Kinez and Mare? How did you find out their names? Did you find that out at the time or 14 years later?

utterances.speaker: VILIM KARLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I found out at the time. I mean, we communicated in a normal way. They talked to me.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: Thank you very much. When you were describing Kinez at the Belgrade Ovcara trial on the 13th of September, 2005, you said on page 7 that he had a camouflage uniform, that's what you said, that he had a blue beret with a red star on it, with a red pointed star. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: VILIM KARLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: In the case in which you testified, or actually in the statement you gave to the Prosecution here in The Hague on page 5, paragraph 2, you said that at Ovcara a captain entered together with Stuka, about whom you said that he had a camouflage uniform and a five-pointed red star on his cap. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: VILIM KARLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: Can we agree that this coincidence is very interesting, that twice you were saved by a person in different places dressed in a practically exactly the same way. And is it the same person?

utterances.speaker: VILIM KARLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: If you read it carefully, and if it was written down properly, what I said was --

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, on page 64, line 3, it should say "blue beret," and it says "cap" here. And it's a significant difference, so can we correct that in the transcript? And I would like to thank the interpreters.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] May I say something?

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: Well, I wasn't following what you said, so you have to start from the beginning.

utterances.speaker: VILIM KARLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It doesn't matter. What I said was something distinctive. The person in the uniform had a moustache. I don't know whether I mentioned that before or not, but this is a fact.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: Very well. Did you meet anybody in Ovcara in a camouflage uniform, a blue beret and a five-pointed red star?

utterances.speaker: VILIM KARLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't remember.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: Did you meet such a person at Velepromet other than Kinez?

utterances.speaker: VILIM KARLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't think that I did. I don't remember.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: Did you meet a person in Mitrovica who was dressed like this or not?

utterances.speaker: VILIM KARLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I cannot remember.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: Well, when you are mentioning the moustache, and this is something that you mentioned for the first time yesterday, there is no statement, and you have three in front of you, where you were describing the captain, you did not say in any of them that this person had a moustache until yesterday. I can read all the statements out to you. You said that he had a dark complexion, but the moustache you mentioned yesterday for the first time.

utterances.speaker: VILIM KARLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can agree with you that perhaps I didn't mention the moustache. Perhaps this wasn't record, but here, before this Trial Chamber and under oath, I stand by the statement that the person who was with Stuka, who was the captain, who told me to step aside, had a moustache.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: And he was 35 to 40 years old. Is that your estimate?

utterances.speaker: VILIM KARLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that is correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: So who actually released you from the hangar? Was it the person in the blue beret, or Stuka? What do you think? What is your assessment?

utterances.speaker: VILIM KARLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was released by Stuka, and also for sure that man with the blue beret. God also has a considerable part in my release with the other people and in my being saved.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: Well, I'm glad to hear of that. Did you ever look for Stuka after Ovcara, since you knew the street where he lived, and the name of the street is -- actually, could you please remind me what the name is?

utterances.speaker: VILIM KARLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I said that I think that my friend lived in a street named Partizanskih Odreda Street.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: Very well. And since Stuka specified where he lived, in 15 years did you try to find such a key person or not?

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] For the witness and for the Prosecution, I have in front of me two documents. I would like one of the documents to be shown an the screen. This is document 2D08-0043. This is the B/C/S version. The English version bears the number 2D08-0047. It's a document that was discovered by the Prosecution. Could we look at page 1 of the document, please? Thank you. Can you zoom -- or are you scroll down a little bit? Thank you. Actually, can we look at the bottom now?

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: Actually, do you see the document?

utterances.speaker: VILIM KARLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: Do you see that it says in the signature a Senior Brigadier Markica Rebic?

utterances.speaker: VILIM KARLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: My question is: Do you know who Markica Rebic is? Have you heard of him?

utterances.speaker: VILIM KARLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: What can you tell us about him?

utterances.speaker: VILIM KARLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Nothing more than what you know about him. I know that he is a senior officer of the Croatian army. I didn't even know that he was a deputy minister. I didn't know that he worked in the information service.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: You gave a statement probably to the Croatian army information service; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: VILIM KARLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: That service, which is part of this ministry, and it says in the letterhead that it's the defence ministry, Zagreb?

utterances.speaker: VILIM KARLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes, correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: Could we look at page 2, please, of this same document. Can we zoom in on the document, please? At the top it said Ministry of Defence, Zagreb; is that correct? Can you please read what it says? If you can, could you please read this?

utterances.speaker: VILIM KARLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: "Republic of Croatia, Ministry of Defence, Zagreb, Security and Information Service Administration."

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: Very well. So that we don't have to go into closed session now, it mentions the case and other names. Could we please scroll down? Do you see the names from the fifth line from the bottom that are mentioned there? Next to your name, do you see your name, Vilim Karlovic?

utterances.speaker: VILIM KARLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, can we go into semi-private session so that I don't improvise when I'm showing this document? Perhaps it will be easier if we go into private session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Private.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. So you spent two days giving an interview to the employees of the defence ministry before you came to testify in The Hague; is that right?

utterances.speaker: VILIM KARLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: Did you sign that statement at the end?

utterances.speaker: VILIM KARLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't remember. Most likely I did.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. After you gave this statement did you, upon arriving here, sleep in the same hotel as other witnesses whose names I'm not going to mention?

utterances.speaker: VILIM KARLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think so.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: Did you stay in that hotel throughout your stay here while giving testimony?

utterances.speaker: VILIM KARLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: Who was the first to testify? No, I apologise. After the first person completed testimony, did that person return to the hotel?

utterances.speaker: VILIM KARLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't remember.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: Did you contact the other witnesses? Did you agree in advance who was going say what?

utterances.speaker: VILIM KARLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's ridiculous. Each person has his or her own story. What was I supposed to agree on with Dr. Vesna Bosanac?

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: After one of the witnesses came to The Hague to testify and then returned back to Amsterdam, were you then spending time together?

utterances.speaker: VILIM KARLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think so.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I think that it's time for our break, but before we break, could we see document 2D08-0051 on the screen, please? We also have the English version, 2D08-0073.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: Do you see the document? Do you see the document?

utterances.speaker: VILIM KARLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, the Prosecution disclosed one page of this document to us. Since this is a part of the entire document under Roman V, I would like to read out what it says here. It says under paragraph Roman V of this document, the title, "Preparing the witness to testify before the International Criminal Court." And then it says that this service took part in preparing the witness to testify in order to confirm the indictment against Mrksic, Radic, Sljivancanin, as well as in the trial against Dokmanovic. And then in parentheses, there is your name, and then Witness Berghofer and (redacted)

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] All right. The page I'm putting to the witness is under 2D08-0064. English version 2D08-0084.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: My question is -- I have all of these versions. Is it true that you gave statements to this service concerning your preparation to testify in the cases before The Hague Tribunal?

utterances.speaker: VILIM KARLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I gave my statement, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: And your statement pertained to what I described?

utterances.speaker: VILIM KARLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is the first time I'm seeing this. I can confirm that I did have an interview with these persons and I told you so myself.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, on this same page, under paragraph 6, it says: "Lacking intelligence support, the service conducted its own analyses and operations and carried out an intelligence break into the International Criminal Court."

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: Since I put all of this to you, and since you agreed that I could be right --

utterances.speaker: VILIM KARLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can't agree about the last thing.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: I'm not asking you about that. My question is: During those two days, were you suggested that some information pertaining to the Croatian state security is something that you are not allowed to disclose?

utterances.speaker: VILIM KARLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: First of all, nobody suggested anything to me. I was just told that I could tell my truth, and my truth was sufficient for everything that was relevant.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: All right. In that case, I will not proceed with these questions.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I would just like to tender this into evidence and then we can conclude with the cross-examination because I see that it's time for the break.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Are you saying you've finished your cross-examination or ...

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] If you allow me to have this document tendered into evidence, then yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: It will be received.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, this document will be marked with number 299 as an exhibit.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I apologise. I put two documents to the witness, the first one and the second one, and I think that they need to be tendered as two separate documents.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: You mean the two languages separately or two distinct documents?

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No. Two different documents. I can read them out again. We had the first one on the screen, and then we had the second one. Both of them have the English and the B/C/S version. So numbers 2D08-0047, that's the English version, and the B/C/S is 2D08-0043. That's the B/C/S version and that's the first document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Can you remind me what was the nature of that document?

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, these are the documents of the information service of the Croatian defence ministry. The first document speaks of parts of the statements given by these persons. It mentions the names of witnesses who were protected. And then the second document had paragraphs 5 and 6, which I put to the witness. I am waiting to hear your decision pertaining to the first document, and then I will tell you about the second document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: My difficulty is because I thought everything was from the one document. I hadn't realised you were dealing with two different documents. But if they are two different documents, they will both be received.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] That's correct.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: And in both languages.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honour, the second document will be marked with number 300 as an exhibit.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Borovic. Now we must break for half an hour, because of the redactions. We will resume at 10 minutes past 6.00. Before we do, Mr. Lukic, will you need more time than will be available to you? Oh, it's Mr. Bulatovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. BULATOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I hope that I will be able to comply with your instructions and to conclude with my cross-examination so that we can release the witness and have a break ourselves.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: With that smile on your face, I have every faith in you, Mr. Bulatovic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Mr. Bulatovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. BULATOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour. Good afternoon to everyone in the courtroom.

utterances.speaker: MR. BULATOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good afternoon to you, Mr. Karlovic.

utterances.speaker: VILIM KARLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Good afternoon.

utterances.speaker: MR. BULATOVIC
utterances.text: I am Momcilo Bulatovic, one of the Defence counsel of Mr. Sljivancanin. Let me just give you the same caution that my colleagues gave before me. Both of us speak the same language, so we should try to make pauses. Mr. Karlovic, there is something in your statements which remains unclear to me. When testifying here, and also in your statements, you said that you came to the hospital on the 17th or 18th; is that right?

utterances.speaker: VILIM KARLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It's possible.

utterances.speaker: MR. BULATOVIC
utterances.text: However, when you testified before the special court in Belgrade, before the war crimes chamber there, you said there that you entered the hospital the night before you were taken to Ovcara, which would mean the 19th?

utterances.speaker: VILIM KARLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It's possible that I said that. Most likely I did say that.

utterances.speaker: MR. BULATOVIC
utterances.text: Well, that's precisely I want to clarify. When did you enter the hospital? I need to clarify that because of some other matters that I will be asking you about.

utterances.speaker: VILIM KARLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I know that I spent at least two nights at the hospital, maybe even three. It's hard for me to be more specific than that. In my recent statements I focused on the 17th.

utterances.speaker: MR. BULATOVIC
utterances.text: I fully realise that; that's why I'm asking you. I know it's been many years, and I can certainly understand. In your evidence you said that you saw Mr. Sljivancanin on the 20th in the morning; is that right?

utterances.speaker: VILIM KARLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, the 20th.

utterances.speaker: MR. BULATOVIC
utterances.text: You saw him in front of the Vukovar Hospital. Please tell me in front of which entrance. Was it the main entrance or the entrance through which you went out?

utterances.speaker: VILIM KARLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The so-called back entrance. I saw him where I was. That's where I saw him.

utterances.speaker: MR. BULATOVIC
utterances.text: Can you specify the time? I know it's very difficult to give us the accurate time, but roughly.

utterances.speaker: VILIM KARLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I will give you a range. Either it was from 8.30 or 9.00 in the morning until 11.00 or 12.00 in the morning. Somewhere in that period of time.

utterances.speaker: MR. BULATOVIC
utterances.text: Did you just see him, was it just visual contact, or did you perhaps talk to him?

utterances.speaker: VILIM KARLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, no. I didn't talk to Mr. Sljivancanin at all.

utterances.speaker: MR. BULATOVIC
utterances.text: After your visual contact, which lasted for several minutes, did you see what he did next? Did you see whether he went somewhere and, if so, where?

utterances.speaker: VILIM KARLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I remember that Mr. Sljivancanin appeared there briefly. I heard a voice yelling at some lieutenant to the effect, "Come on, hurry up, what are you waiting for?" And then I lifted my head up and saw Mr. Sljivancanin there. He stayed up to one minute, and then he went back to the entrance.

utterances.speaker: MR. BULATOVIC
utterances.text: Did you see whether he entered the hospital?

utterances.speaker: VILIM KARLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I didn't see. I didn't look for that matter either.

utterances.speaker: MR. BULATOVIC
utterances.text: So from that moment on you never saw Mr. Sljivancanin live again?

utterances.speaker: VILIM KARLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I didn't.

utterances.speaker: MR. BULATOVIC
utterances.text: Now let's focus on how people boarded the buses, the buses that were parked as you explained to us. Was there anyone by the buses issuing orders to you as to how to board buses, or did you do it based on how people reached buses?

utterances.speaker: VILIM KARLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: There was a column in front of the hospital and it was specified how many people should board the bus. The JNA soldiers accompanied us to the buses.

utterances.speaker: MR. BULATOVIC
utterances.text: Does it mean that the selection, if we can call it this way, was based on the number of people that the buses could hold, that no other criteria were used?

utterances.speaker: VILIM KARLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Most likely that's correct, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. BULATOVIC
utterances.text: Let us now turn to your arrival at the hospital. Today you said that you had gone to the hospital previously to visit some of your wounded comrades?

utterances.speaker: VILIM KARLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. BULATOVIC
utterances.text: I would like to know whether you had any contact with somebody at the hospital, either Dr. Bosanac or Dr. Njavro?

utterances.speaker: VILIM KARLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I personally never had any contact with them.

utterances.speaker: MR. BULATOVIC
utterances.text: Did you have contact with any other doctor at the hospital in order to inquire about the health of your fellow combatants?

utterances.speaker: VILIM KARLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. No, I had no such contact. All of my combatants were conscious, and I could get any information I needed from them directly.

utterances.speaker: MR. BULATOVIC
utterances.text: When you came to the hospital, did you see whether there were armed guards at the hospital?

utterances.speaker: VILIM KARLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can't remember that. You mean inside the hospital?

utterances.speaker: MR. BULATOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: VILIM KARLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can't remember that.

utterances.speaker: MR. BULATOVIC
utterances.text: That day when you came to the hospital, the 17th, the 18th, we don't need to be specific, were there other civilians at the hospital -- no, I mean were there civilians at all at the hospital, and did some civilians arrive after you?

utterances.speaker: VILIM KARLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: There were civilians, and new ones arrived as well.

utterances.speaker: MR. BULATOVIC
utterances.text: All right. Can you put a number how many civilians were there on the 20th? On the 20th in the morning, how many civilians were there in the hospital?

utterances.speaker: VILIM KARLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I couldn't give you a number, but there was a great deal of people.

utterances.speaker: MR. BULATOVIC
utterances.text: Do you know that on the 19th in the evening there was an evacuation of civilians from the Vukovar Hospital organised by the Croatian Red Cross?

utterances.speaker: VILIM KARLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's the first I hear of it. I never heard of any evacuation of civilians on the 19th.

utterances.speaker: MR. BULATOVIC
utterances.text: Did you ever hear of a person called Zeljka Zgonjanin?

utterances.speaker: VILIM KARLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Never in my life.

utterances.speaker: MR. BULATOVIC
utterances.text: You spoke of a group of people that was under your command. It was either a platoon or a detachment. It numbered 10 people. Mr. Borovic asked you about other volunteers from Croatia. I'm now interested in the composition of the group numbering 21 men. Were they from different towns in Croatia or from the same town?

utterances.speaker: VILIM KARLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Let me see if I can remember. Most of them were from Zagreb. Let's say half of the group was from Zagreb. Some people were from Slavonia. I think that these two groups made up the entire group.

utterances.speaker: MR. BULATOVIC
utterances.text: Can you tell us something about the age of the members of that group? Were they all your peers, were they older than you?

utterances.speaker: VILIM KARLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The only senior members in terms of age were Zeljko Major and Nemec who went missing at Ovcara, and the rest of us were all aged --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: The interpreters didn't hear the age range.

utterances.speaker: MR. BULATOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Karlovic, let us clarify something else that remains not entirely clear.

utterances.speaker: MR. BULATOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, on page 78, line 17 -- no, I apologise, 16, the witness said that the age range was similar. They were all born within three to five years.

utterances.speaker: MR. BULATOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Karlovic, you mentioned somebody called Tihomir Perkovic; is that right?

utterances.speaker: VILIM KARLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I need to add something.

utterances.speaker: MR. BULATOVIC
utterances.text: Please go ahead.

utterances.speaker: VILIM KARLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I told the Prosecutor that I wasn't sure whether his first name was Tihomir. Perkovic is his last name, but I'm not sure about his first name.

utterances.speaker: MR. BULATOVIC
utterances.text: When Mr. Domazet was examining you, you said that he returned to Vukovar [as interpreted]. He was the leader of the group of 21 that included you.

utterances.speaker: VILIM KARLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. BULATOVIC
utterances.text: And there was a Perkovic person at Ovcara as well. Is that the same man?

utterances.speaker: VILIM KARLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. They only share their last name. And I even believe that their first names were the same as well.

utterances.speaker: MR. BULATOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Another intervention for the transcript, page 78, line 5. The question was that Perkovic came back from Vukovar rather than returning to Vukovar, just by way of clarification.

utterances.speaker: MR. BULATOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Karlovic, did you hear anything about the surrender of the Mitnica battalion when you were at the hospital?

utterances.speaker: VILIM KARLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. I heard about it later and I can explain, perhaps.

utterances.speaker: MR. BULATOVIC
utterances.text: Whilst you were at the Vukovar Hospital did you hear of any attempts to break through by the Vukovar defenders and that a part of it was unsuccessful and that those people ended up at the Vukovar Hospital?

utterances.speaker: VILIM KARLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know anything about that.

utterances.speaker: MR. BULATOVIC
utterances.text: You said that you came to the Vukovar barracks after about an hour, after you were boarded on the buses next to the hospital?

utterances.speaker: VILIM KARLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Counting from the moment when we started being lined up and separated and boarded on to the buses, in my estimate, it lasted for about an hour.

utterances.speaker: MR. BULATOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I would kindly ask for Exhibit 256, photograph number 13, to be shown to the witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. BULATOVIC
utterances.text: Can you see this photograph?

utterances.speaker: VILIM KARLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I can.

utterances.speaker: MR. BULATOVIC
utterances.text: Can you recognise the facility shown?

utterances.speaker: VILIM KARLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Now I know what it is, but I can't remember too many details. The large hangar reminds me of the place where we were on the buses.

utterances.speaker: MR. BULATOVIC
utterances.text: As regards the hangar, what facility is that a part of? Because we spoke about Ovcara and Velepromet.

utterances.speaker: VILIM KARLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The largest hangar reminds me of the place where we were with the buses.

utterances.speaker: MR. BULATOVIC
utterances.text: But I'm interested in the location. Where that hangar is. Is this Velepromet or the barracks or Ovcara?

utterances.speaker: VILIM KARLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: There is a possibility that this is the Vukovar barracks.

utterances.speaker: MR. BULATOVIC
utterances.text: I will kindly ask the assistance of the usher to provide a pen for the witness. Since you said that the largest hangar reminds you of the place where the buses were stopped, could you please mark the buses as to how they were stopped when you finally reached the barracks? You can draw the lines the same way you did before.

utterances.speaker: VILIM KARLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks]. This was approximately so.

utterances.speaker: MR. BULATOVIC
utterances.text: Could you put the letter A next to the lines.

utterances.speaker: VILIM KARLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks].

utterances.speaker: MR. BULATOVIC
utterances.text: Please mark your bus with the letter B.

utterances.speaker: VILIM KARLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks].

utterances.speaker: MR. BULATOVIC
utterances.text: If we take this to be your bus, could you please mark your approximate position on that bus using a small cross?

utterances.speaker: VILIM KARLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: If we are to deal further with this photograph, although I am unsure as to what it shows, I must say that the position of my bus was not exactly this way, as I marked it as being the fourth bus. Also, I can't remember with a degree of certainty that I was on the fourth bus at the barracks, but I do remember when I disembarked at Ovcara I was on the fourth bus. Please take that into account. I don't know how to mark where I was seated, but I was seated behind the driver, next to the window.

utterances.speaker: MR. BULATOVIC
utterances.text: The front part of the buses, was that in the direction of the arrow?

utterances.speaker: VILIM KARLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The position of my bus was more or less where the third line is, if you understand me. I did put the lines there, but I believe the most accurate reflection would be the middle line.

utterances.speaker: MR. BULATOVIC
utterances.text: I understand. I believe that colour -- that pen comes in a different colour as well. Perhaps you can use the blue one to mark your position on the bus. I believe it was on the left side, if you were seated behind the driver.

utterances.speaker: VILIM KARLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The pen doesn't put the cross at an exact place where I intended to.

utterances.speaker: MR. BULATOVIC
utterances.text: I believe this is sufficient. Could you please mark the spot with the letter C.

utterances.speaker: VILIM KARLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks].

utterances.speaker: MR. BULATOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. From the place where you were, you commanded the view of the interior part, did you not?

utterances.speaker: VILIM KARLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. BULATOVIC
utterances.text: Did you see the arrival of any other bus?

utterances.speaker: VILIM KARLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can't remember whether that bus came subsequently or whether it had already been at the barracks. I confused that particular situation. I can mark it in blue where I think the bus was, but as I say, I'm not certain when it arrived.

utterances.speaker: MR. BULATOVIC
utterances.text: Please mark the position of the bus, and as for whether it was there already or whether it came later, we can discuss that further.

utterances.speaker: VILIM KARLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks]. Well, again, the pen put the mark in a somewhat different place than I intended to.

utterances.speaker: MR. BULATOVIC
utterances.text: Could you please mark that with the letter D.

utterances.speaker: VILIM KARLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks].

utterances.speaker: MR. BULATOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, could we please tender this photograph.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: It will be received.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, this will be exhibit number 301.

utterances.speaker: MR. BULATOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. BULATOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Karlovic, concerning the place where you were and the bus you saw later, I want to know the following: Did you see anyone being taken off your bus?

utterances.speaker: VILIM KARLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: As far as I can recall, it seems to me that no one was taken off my bus.

utterances.speaker: MR. BULATOVIC
utterances.text: Did you see anyone being taken from any of the other buses?

utterances.speaker: VILIM KARLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I did.

utterances.speaker: MR. BULATOVIC
utterances.text: Which one?

utterances.speaker: VILIM KARLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The bus that was behind us. I saw people being taken off and they passed next to our bus.

utterances.speaker: MR. BULATOVIC
utterances.text: And they were taken where?

utterances.speaker: VILIM KARLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: To the bus I marked with the blue line.

utterances.speaker: MR. BULATOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Karlovic, when you went towards Ovcara, did all the buses leave together, including the fifth -- the blue one? Did you see that? If you didn't, please don't speculate.

utterances.speaker: VILIM KARLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I wouldn't want to speculate. I know that our buses left, and that particular bus, I know that he appeared subsequently at Ovcara. Perhaps to clarify: The bus pretty much like the one I saw at the barracks, because it seems that every word counts here.

utterances.speaker: MR. BULATOVIC
utterances.text: Apart from the people being taken off the bus you mentioned and then put on another bus, did you see anyone else being taken off?

utterances.speaker: VILIM KARLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can't remember anything else. I know what I told you.

utterances.speaker: MR. BULATOVIC
utterances.text: Let us now move to Ovcara. You arrived there, and you told Mr. Borovic what the position of the buses was. Apart from the buses parked there the way you described, did you notice any other vehicles, parked vehicles? Were there any other civilian vehicles? And if your answer is yes, then I will have further questions.

utterances.speaker: VILIM KARLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Are we talking about Ovcara?

utterances.speaker: MR. BULATOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: VILIM KARLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I spoke about that yesterday. And this is what I can recall sitting here today. I remember some military vehicles in front of the hangar.

utterances.speaker: MR. BULATOVIC
utterances.text: Do you remember any civilian vehicles?

utterances.speaker: VILIM KARLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I no longer recall.

utterances.speaker: MR. BULATOVIC
utterances.text: I'm interested in the moment when you entered the Ovcara hangar in which, according to your statement, you spent some three to four minutes?

utterances.speaker: VILIM KARLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I believe so.

utterances.speaker: MR. BULATOVIC
utterances.text: We also heard what you saw there. Could you please describe for us the situation in the hangar, what happened to those people who were taken off the buses and put into the hangar? Were they seated, were they standing, lying on the ground?

utterances.speaker: VILIM KARLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: They were placed against the wall with their arms and legs spread apart.

utterances.speaker: MR. BULATOVIC
utterances.text: Did you notice that perhaps there was some sort of a separation line between the people in -- or among the people in the hangar? Was there any sort of rope or anything else?

utterances.speaker: VILIM KARLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: What do you mean a separation line?

utterances.speaker: MR. BULATOVIC
utterances.text: A separation line inside the hangar. For example, that some people were divided in one part of the hangar and the others in the other part and separated by a rope.

utterances.speaker: VILIM KARLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't recall anything of that nature.

utterances.speaker: MR. BULATOVIC
utterances.text: When you were taken out of the hangar, as you described, having spent some time at the place you marked in answering to Mr. Borovic's questions, I wanted to know the following: The six men who were there with you, had they been there before you came, or did they come after you?

utterances.speaker: VILIM KARLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't remember whether all of them had already been outside, but some of them were. I can't remember whether I was the last one to arrive or the one before last.

utterances.speaker: MR. BULATOVIC
utterances.text: So you spent an hour and a half, up to two hours there?

utterances.speaker: VILIM KARLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, maybe even two hours.

utterances.speaker: MR. BULATOVIC
utterances.text: Did you communicate amongst yourselves?

utterances.speaker: VILIM KARLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. We could.

utterances.speaker: MR. BULATOVIC
utterances.text: In talking to those people, did you hear of any people who were deserters from the JNA?

utterances.speaker: VILIM KARLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is the first time I hear of it.

utterances.speaker: MR. BULATOVIC
utterances.text: Did you see any JNA officer take out any of the prisoners from the hangar? We heard who took you out of the hangar, but apart from that, was there anything else, apart --

utterances.speaker: VILIM KARLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: There may have been such instances, but I don't remember.

utterances.speaker: MR. BULATOVIC
utterances.text: As regards the bus when you were on it, did you hear of any people on your bus who deserted from the JNA?

utterances.speaker: VILIM KARLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't remember that, because I probably didn't find that important at the time.

utterances.speaker: MR. BULATOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Karlovic, in answering to one of Mr. Domazet's questions -- question, you said that a part of your statement pertains to your impressions and what you thought you may have seen, particularly with a view of the time that elapsed. You explained the uniforms and your conclusions as to who could have been from what group, et cetera. You also said that you knew something about the existence of the Vukovar TO.

utterances.speaker: VILIM KARLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I knew what I was able to conclude in terms of who belonged to what group.

utterances.speaker: MR. BULATOVIC
utterances.text: Could you explain the uniforms and insignia of the Vukovar TO?

utterances.speaker: VILIM KARLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can't say anything more than I already did. I can repeat if you want me to.

utterances.speaker: MR. BULATOVIC
utterances.text: No, that won't be necessary. I just hoped you could explain it in more detail. As you said, there were all types of uniforms. Parts of uniforms were mixed as well. Would you allow for a possibility that your opinion as to who belonged to what group may be wrong?

utterances.speaker: VILIM KARLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: If you are asking me about a possibility of me being wrong, yes, of course I may be.

utterances.speaker: MR. BULATOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, particularly having in mind the time that passed and the state of stress that you were under at the time, it could have affected your memory?

utterances.speaker: VILIM KARLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I guess so.

utterances.speaker: MR. BULATOVIC
utterances.text: You have said that the barracks commander came to Velepromet and that he took you away in his Opel Omega car. Did you have any conversation with him whilst driving in his car? Were you able to explain anything to him, explain your situation? Because as far as I understood, he didn't put you on the bus precisely because of your situation and the condition you were in.

utterances.speaker: VILIM KARLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I remember having spoken to a soldier who was a part of the security detail of the aforementioned officer, and as far as I recall, I did not speak with the commander. I did talk to the soldier who was seated at the back together with me.

utterances.speaker: MR. BULATOVIC
utterances.text: What date was that?

utterances.speaker: VILIM KARLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was supposed to be the 21st of November.

utterances.speaker: MR. BULATOVIC
utterances.text: You said that you noticed a small clock in the car?

utterances.speaker: VILIM KARLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I remember that clock clearly that was inside the Opel Omega.

utterances.speaker: MR. BULATOVIC
utterances.text: So can you tell us what the time was?

utterances.speaker: VILIM KARLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: 20 minutes to midnight. Perhaps it's strange and silly, but --

utterances.speaker: MR. BULATOVIC
utterances.text: No, no, no, it's not that at all. After that you spent the night at the Vukovar barracks, and then you were transferred by the articulated bus to Sremska Mitrovica where you provided some eight to 10 statements?

utterances.speaker: VILIM KARLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, you don't have to take it exactly like that.

utterances.speaker: MR. BULATOVIC
utterances.text: You were questioned several times. What I would like to know is whether you wrote a statement out by hand and, if you did, how many times did you do that?

utterances.speaker: VILIM KARLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, we all wrote out statements, but I don't remember. I think that I wrote out a statement at least twice, but I'm not sure.

utterances.speaker: MR. BULATOVIC
