utterances.text: While you were in Sremska Mitrovica, were you visited by a representative of the International Red Cross?

utterances.speaker: VILIM KARLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I was registered some two months later, because for a while I was concealed from the International Red Cross at the Sremska Mitrovica camp.

utterances.speaker: MR. BULATOVIC
utterances.text: Did you write, fill in or in any way communicate with representatives of the Red Cross?

utterances.speaker: VILIM KARLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. BULATOVIC
utterances.text: Did you fill in a questionnaire?

utterances.speaker: VILIM KARLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: On the 16th of January was the first time that I was registered by the Red Cross, if I can recall.

utterances.speaker: MR. BULATOVIC
utterances.text: This questionnaire, did you fill it in or did someone else fill it in?

utterances.speaker: VILIM KARLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think that I did.

utterances.speaker: MR. BULATOVIC
utterances.text: Do you recall the kind of information that it contained? What did you need to enter into the questionnaire?

utterances.speaker: VILIM KARLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Name, first name, last name, name of -- father's name, perhaps something else, but I don't remember.

utterances.speaker: MR. BULATOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Karlovic, I heard here today that you are retired with disability?

utterances.speaker: VILIM KARLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. BULATOVIC
utterances.text: I'm interested in something else. Were you continuously in the army until 2002?

utterances.speaker: VILIM KARLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. BULATOVIC
utterances.text: And what is the reason why you retired with disability, the reason why you retired. You state as the reason you retired as illness. Can you tell us what it is?

utterances.speaker: VILIM KARLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Do I have to speak about my illness before this Trial Chamber?

utterances.speaker: MR. BULATOVIC
utterances.text: I'm not going to insist on that.

utterances.speaker: VILIM KARLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I do reserve the right not to talk about my illness. I can, I mean ...

utterances.speaker: MR. BULATOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Karlovic, you have said that the person who saved your life at Ovcara, in a way, that you never actually sought that person ever?

utterances.speaker: VILIM KARLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I did not.

utterances.speaker: MR. BULATOVIC
utterances.text: Did you ever make inquiries about him using the nickname that he told you?

utterances.speaker: VILIM KARLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I didn't really make inquiries. I didn't try to contact anyone in Serbia who would be able to help me to reach this Stuka, whose first name was Ilija.

utterances.speaker: MR. BULATOVIC
utterances.text: I heard today that you had information about Milojevic, Kinez, that he was -- proceedings were being conducted in his -- in Croatia for crimes that he committed?

utterances.speaker: VILIM KARLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I seem to remember something like that in the press about Predrag Milojevic, Kinez.

utterances.speaker: MR. BULATOVIC
utterances.text: Did you try to find out in any other way, other than through the newspaper, whether it was the same Kinez? Did you try to go through any security services of the Republic of Croatia or some other organs? Did you try to gather information about that?

utterances.speaker: VILIM KARLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm going to answer that. Earlier I said that I didn't really pay attention to that, because I didn't believe that it was that same person, because of the way he acted towards me.

utterances.speaker: MR. BULATOVIC
utterances.text: When you were talking about Stuka -- actually, when you talked with Stuka at Ovcara, did you exchange particulars or anything?

utterances.speaker: VILIM KARLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: As far as I can remember, no.

utterances.speaker: MR. BULATOVIC
utterances.text: Let me ask you this: Can you explain to me how was it that you were proposed as a witness before the tribunal in Belgrade or the court in Belgrade? How did the defence counsel get to you? How did they get in touch for you?

utterances.speaker: VILIM KARLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Later I found out they were looking for me for a long time, but since I was building a house, I was registered at one address, lived at another, and I was making my house or building my house at some third location, I don't know how, probably through the Croatian justice ministry, they managed to get my new address. And the defence lawyer managed to do that after I had registered at the address where I was building my house. So the defence counsel of Marko Ljuboja, Mare, reached me, and he called me and asked me if I was willing to testify.

utterances.speaker: MR. BULATOVIC
utterances.text: I understand all of that. What I'm interested in is how did they know your first and last name? How did they know how to look for?

utterances.speaker: VILIM KARLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know either, but I can tell you what I learned later. There were other witnesses and somebody mentioned me by name at the trial and they described my case. So that is probably how Mare himself, and Kinez, during the trial, concluded that it could probably be me. And that is why their defence counsel got in touch with me. They weren't sure it was me at first. They spoke with me first.

utterances.speaker: MR. BULATOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Karlovic, one of my first questions was that you never saw Mr. Sljivancanin live other than on the 20th in the morning at -- between 9.00 and 11.00 that morning. You said that after your release, I think that was on the 22nd of May, if I'm not mistaken. You said that later you saw him frequently on Croatian television?

utterances.speaker: VILIM KARLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, at least once a year.

utterances.speaker: MR. BULATOVIC
utterances.text: What I would like to know is: What were these programmes where you saw Mr. Sljivancanin?

utterances.speaker: VILIM KARLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can tell you that Mr. Sljivancanin was shown most often as he was arguing from that gentleman from the European Union or commission or community or whatever.

utterances.speaker: MR. BULATOVIC
utterances.text: What was the context in which this was shown or broadcast? Can you tell me whether it was in a positive or a negative context?

utterances.speaker: VILIM KARLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, what else could I say other than it was in a negative context.

utterances.speaker: MR. BULATOVIC
utterances.text: Did this perhaps help to form a kind of public opinion or attitude towards Mr. Sljivancanin, as well as yours?

utterances.speaker: VILIM KARLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, nobody will ever influence my attitude or position.

utterances.speaker: MR. BULATOVIC
utterances.text: Well, I'm not thinking of you specifically. I mean, but you don't live all by yourself. You live in a specific context?

utterances.speaker: VILIM KARLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know how else to answer this question. Mr. Sljivancanin was not a positive figure in Croatia. And I told you about my position. The only thing that I want is the truth. I don't want any innocent Serbs being put into prison.

utterances.speaker: MR. BULATOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, thank you very much. I have no further questions for this witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you very much, Mr. Bulatovic. Mr. Smith.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: Your Honour, probably something you don't want to hear. I have approximately 10 minutes, I would say, of re-examination. I would try and be as fast as I can and --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Press on, Mr. Smith.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: Witness, I would just like to make a couple of clarifications after your cross-examination. It was put to you by my learned friend, Mr. Domazet, that the first time that you mentioned that JNA soldiers were involved in the gauntlet at Ovcara was when you testified yesterday. I would just now like to read to you a passage from the Rule 61 hearing which was on the 27th of March, 1996 when you testified, and I would like you to comment on that when I finish. You were -- on page 306 you were discussing what had happened at Ovcara, and a question was put to you by the prosecutor and the question was: "Were you able to see what was happening to the people getting off the buses in front of you?" And the answer recorded from you was: "I saw that in front of the hangar there was a file. There were ranks consisting of Chetniks and JNA soldiers. They took away parts of the clothing, took away documents, money from the people, any gold objects which people might have had. They threw their clothes on to a pile, but especially what I noticed that as people passed through these two ranks, they were beaten very, very badly." Your explanation continues after that. But the question I'll put to you is: Do you remember making that statement or a statement similar to that when you first testified here at the Tribunal in 1996?

utterances.speaker: VILIM KARLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: To this day, I continue to assert that this is what I stated. That is my statement.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: Thank you. I will now provide you a copy of your statement that you gave in 1995 with the assistance of the usher. And this is the statement that you gave to the Prosecution investigators. In fact, I believe you might have the English one in front of you; is that correct? You have the B/C/S one?

utterances.speaker: VILIM KARLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, no.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: It was put to you that there was some suggestion why you haven't mentioned what occurred at Velepromet and the incident in relation to Kinez and Mare, why that hadn't been mentioned before, and only first discussed at the Belgrade trial. Can you read the last sentence of that statement, please?

utterances.speaker: VILIM KARLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: "If necessary, I am willing to provide another statement about events that occurred in Velepromet." I will be sincere. I really cannot recall saying that, but I must have said it because I did mention Velepromet also the first time.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: And when you were questioned at the Tribunal in the two cases previous to this one, at this Tribunal, were you ever asked questions by the Prosecutor in detail as to what happened at Velepromet or what happened when you were taken from there to the house that Kinez and Mare rescued you from?

utterances.speaker: VILIM KARLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I cannot remember whether I provided a statement about events at Velepromet before the Trial Chamber. I cannot remember.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: I would also like to put a couple of questions to you in relation to how you got to Vukovar from Zagreb. It was put to you that you were under no combat or no fire when you left from Bogdanovci to reach the silos. Do you remember saying that in cross-examination?

utterances.speaker: VILIM KARLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: And you said in examination-in-chief that you got off the bus at Bogdanovci and then went to the silos, and to get to the silos you went through the cornfields. Do you remember stating that?

utterances.speaker: VILIM KARLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: Can you explain to the Court why the bus didn't take you directly to the silos and you went on foot through the cornfields to get there?

utterances.speaker: VILIM KARLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: For the simple reason that we would be noticed if we were using any kind of vehicle. The town was blocked and all you could do is enter the town in small groups on foot.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: And it was also -- I think a date may have been misrecorded in the transcript, but if you can help us with it, and this is at page 48, line 16. You mentioned in answer to a question by my learned friend, Mr. Borovic, that you went to the Vukovar Hospital after leaving your position, your combat position, which was about a hundred metres to 200 metres away from the hospital, and the date that was recorded in the transcript was the 13th of September, 2002. Can you tell the Court what date you left your position and went to the hospital?

utterances.speaker: VILIM KARLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I really don't know where we get the 13th of September. Abide by what I said, that on the 17th I went to the hospital. I really don't know why the 13th. Perhaps it was a mistake, or maybe I said it, but I'm also wondering about the date, the 13th of September.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: You didn't arrive at -- in Vukovar until the 30th of September; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: VILIM KARLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. But I don't know how the 13th of September figures here. I mean, if I heard it properly, but perhaps I can explain it again.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Mr. Borovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I would like to help my learned friend and not confuse the witness. This is the 13th of September when you gave your statement in the Belgrade Ovcara case. I think this will perhaps help to clarify the confusion.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Borovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: And I think the date in the transcript as the 13th of September, 2002. But in any event, the date that you left that last combat position, what date was that?

utterances.speaker: VILIM KARLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I left the combat position on the 17th. This was on the 17th of November, 1991.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: And perhaps there is a little confusion in the transcript at page 54, line 17. Can you tell the Court whether you saw this person Stuka at the JNA barracks or not, or was the first time you saw him at Ovcara?

utterances.speaker: VILIM KARLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I said that the first time I saw him was at Ovcara. I did not see him at the barracks.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: Thank you. And the last question, you said that you sat behind the driver on the bus when you left the hospital. Did you sit directly behind the driver on the left-hand side, or did you sit on the right-hand side; do you remember?

utterances.speaker: VILIM KARLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: On the left side. Very close. I think I was sitting in row two, if I remember correctly.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: And also you stated that when you looked at the photograph of the JNA barracks only a few buildings on that were familiar to you; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: VILIM KARLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I based it on the large hangar and also the actual compound. But I -- I'm not quite sure that that was that particular place.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: And in relation to the parking of the buses, how confident are you that the buses were parked in that location that you marked on the map? You seemed a little uncertain in your answers.

utterances.speaker: VILIM KARLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I warned the Defence -- warned. I mean, I don't need to warn you, but I did say myself that I cannot decidedly say that that was that photograph.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: Your Honour, I have no further questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Smith. Mr. Moore.

utterances.speaker: MR. MOORE
utterances.text: Your Honour, I rise unusually to give some good news. It's quite simply this: The witness Kypr has been here all day. He's been speaking to an interpreter, and the document will be concluded today by way of interpretation, and therefore it should be available tomorrow evening. Now, if we're not sitting obviously tomorrow and Thursday, we have to make arrangements for my learned friends, but certainly it will be available tomorrow afternoon, and so therefore I see no reason why we can't start on Friday, as originally arranged.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you for that and for your efforts, Mr. Moore.

utterances.speaker: MR. MOORE
utterances.text: I have a second point, but I won't detain the Court too long. It really relates to a point for another witness, and I won't deal with it now, but it's at page 6298, and it is the witness, I think it was 009. It really relates to the cross-examination by my learned friend Mr. Lukic putting the case to 009, and if I may just deal with lines 6 and 8, because clearly it's important that there is no ambiguity in relation to this evidence. If I may put it in very general terms, what was said by the witness was that he saw Major Sljivancanin at the JNA barracks and he saw Major Sljivancanin at Ovcara. Mr. Lukic put his case on page 6298, but -- and I don't criticise in any way at all, he says: "That was why you gave the story you did. And this was the background to which you placed my client somewhere where he had never been; is that right?" For my part, I wonder if my learned friend would be kind enough to clarify whether he is suggesting that it is fabricated in relation to the JNA barracks and Ovcara, or does this challenge merely relate to Ovcara? The relevance is obvious for the trial as a whole.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Do you want to deal with that at this moment, Mr. Lukic?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] That's precisely what I was going to ask Your Honours. I can't open that page right now, and therefore I would rather refrain from stating my position. With your permission, I will do that on Friday, once I check the transcript.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you very much. You have to wait, Mr. Moore. Mr. Karlovic, you will be pleased to know that that is the end of your evidence. There are no more questions for you. The Chamber would like to thank you for your attendance here in The Hague, and for the assistance that you have been able to give. You may, of course, now return to your home and your personal affairs. Thank you very much. For the reasons we have discussed, we will resume the hearing on Friday morning at 9.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: to be reconvened on Friday, the 24th day of March, 2006, at 9.00 a.m.

procedural_notes.text: --- Whereupon the hearing adjourned at 7.08 p.m.,
